character_sheet: A small passive fish: a boxy body and head with a mouth and hinged jaw, a dorsal fin, four pectoral fins, a bottom fin, a two-part tail with two caudal fins and two lower bottom fins. It swims in water and is harmless. Read it as a fish that never stops finning: every fin at its own slow rhythm.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig on a 64x64 sheet.

behaviour: Several independent rhythms run at all times, none scaled by walking speed; the classic code has no rest pose. The transcription ships idle (no bone) plus one clip per rhythm: the primary group (`primary_group`; the first group when the seed names none) carries the bare `walk` - a label, not a semantic: the contract's fly -> walk fallback is what plays a flyer's walk in flight (owner 2026-09-13, addendum item 26 (2)) - and every other rhythm is `walk_<group>`, so the GeckoLib candidate plays the transcription behind the switch.

Six rhythms: four pectoral fins each at its own rate (the left front one is the primary group: its clip is the bare walk), the lower fin pair, the jaw; the body, head, tail and caudal fins are static. The pectoral fins bind at -/+0.335 rad about Y and the jaw at -0.228 rad about X, so the transcription's keys carry the offset (base minus bind). The pectoral and lower fins are rotated zero-thickness cubes: the seam lights them by their true normals (ENT-S-161).

The default renderer poses it from the classic code; the GeckoLib candidate sits behind the dev switch (-Dorespawn.dev.geckolibRenderers) and your clips replace the shipped transcription file for file.
